agency: Brevard County Sheriff's Office
text: Stay home and off the roadways unless necessary to travel to and from work or to escape high flooding. US 192 in Melbourne has flooded out. Expect significant delays.

agency: West Melbourne Police
text: Stay off the roads. Roads are flooded and cars are disabled throughout the city. Call 911 for life-or-death emergencies only.

agency: City of Palm Bay
text: Palm Bay City Hall and city offices closed today due to flooding. Widespread flooding in Palm Bay; avoid flooded roadways. Recreation facilities closed; trash collection cancelled today.

agency: Cocoa Beach Police
text: Never drive through standing water; stay indoors during the warning. No specific Cocoa Beach road closures posted.

agency: Brevard County Emergency Management
text: Limit water use: rain plus normal use is stressing the wastewater system (Cocoa Beach lift stations at capacity).

agency: Brevard Public Schools
text: All schools closed today due to flooding.

agency: Space Launch Delta 45 (Patrick SFB / Cape Canaveral SFS)
text: Non-mission-essential personnel should not report today because of hazardous roads and local flooding on base.

agency: City of Titusville
text: Wastewater system at capacity after overnight rain; controlled release of treated reclaimed water into the Indian River Lagoon began about 6:30 a.m. at the Osprey facility. Residents asked to cut nonessential water use (laundry, dishwashers, long showers) until further notice. Some Titusville streets impassable.

agency: Space Coast Area Transit (via WFTV)
text: Routes 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28 and 30 (Melbourne and Palm Bay area) suspended for Monday because of flooding. Routes 26 and 29 running with long delays; long delays on all other routes.

agency: Brevard County Government (via Spectrum News 13)
text: Brevard County government facilities closed countywide today because of flooding; all courts also closed.

agency: City of Palm Bay (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
text: Water shut off to several neighborhoods near Malabar Rd and Port Malabar Blvd after a water main break on Port Malabar Blvd NE; flooding prevents repairs. Boil water notice will apply once service is restored.

agency: City of Palm Bay Mayor (via News 6)
text: Fairhaven area of Palm Bay is inaccessible because of flooding; no specific roads named.

agency: City of Palm Bay (via Spectrum News 13)
text: Palm Bay officials declared a shelter-in-place on Monday morning because heavy rain is flooding streets and roads. Residents are asked to stay home and conserve water. Parts of Port Malabar Rd are washed out after Turkey Creek overflowed.

agency: City of Cocoa Beach (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
text: Waste Management warns that trash and recycling pickup in Cocoa Beach may be delayed because of heavy rain and flooding across Brevard County. City recreation facilities are closed.

agency: City of Melbourne (via The Weather Channel)
text: Melbourne City Hall is closed to the public because of flooding.

agency: City of Melbourne
text: Stay off the roads and shelter in place. Multiple roads closed by flooding, including Dubber Rd, North Dr, Stewart Rd, Dairy Rd at Edgewood Dr, and Edgewood Rd at Ruffner Rd. Avoid affected areas.

agency: State of Florida, Governor's Office (via WFTV)
text: State of emergency declared for Brevard and six other counties (Executive Order 26-227) because of flooding. Effective immediately for 60 days; includes price-gouging protections.

agency: Brevard Public Schools (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
text: Because of the extent of flooding across the county, all Brevard Public Schools campuses and district offices will stay closed Tuesday, Nov. 3. Schools are expected to reopen Wednesday.

agency: Brevard County Supervisor of Elections (via News 6)
text: Because of the historic flooding, some Election Day precinct polling locations are being moved temporarily for Tuesday's General Election. Voters should check where their precinct will vote before going.

agency: Brevard County Emergency Management (via Spectrum News 13)
text: Water on some roads has gone down since earlier in the day, but county officials still ask residents not to leave home unless they absolutely must or are under evacuation orders. The Red Cross has opened a shelter in Cocoa at Parker Memorial Missionary Baptist Church.

agency: Brevard County Supervisor of Elections (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
text: Because of flooding, the Supervisor of Elections offices in Titusville, Melbourne and Palm Bay are closed to the public until further notice. The Viera office at 2725 Judge Fran Jamieson Way is open, and its secure ballot intake station is taking completed mail ballots.
